subject: Action required: evacuation window for US/EU endpoints — Tenant routing opt-in and reroute steps
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: platform-ops@bluefin.io, infra@greenlane.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-19T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Action required: evacuation window for US/EU endpoints — Tenant routing opt-in and reroute steps

Hi team,

We want to notify you of a planned evacuation window that will affect traffic entering our US-East (us-east-1) and EU-West (eu-west-1) regional edge POPs. This is a targeted operational window to remediate an unstable peering fabric in the provider fabric we rely on. The window is planned for:

  - Start: 2026-05-19 22:00 UTC
  - End: 2026-05-20 02:00 UTC

Impact summary: some requests routed through the affected POPs may experience increased latency, transient 5xx errors, or connection resets. Customers who use our global regional routing will see traffic rerouted automatically to healthy POPs when they have "Emergency Reroute" enabled in Console. For tenants without that opt-in enabled, traffic will continue to use your pinned region unless you complete the manual opt-in below.

Action requested (two options):

  1) Opt in to automatic emergency reroute (recommended):
     - Console: Console > Tenant > Traffic Routing > Emergency Reroute -> toggle ON.
     - API: POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/routing/actions with body: {"action":"enable_emergency_reroute"} (bearer token required).
  2) Manual temporary endpoints (if you cannot enable reroute):
     - Update your endpoint to the temporary addresses we provide in the CSV attachment (temporary-endpoints.csv).
     - These endpoints will accept traffic for the evacuation window and forward to healthy capacity.

We will perform canary validation and graceful cutovers; we will never fail closed for tenants that opt out, but opt-out tenants may see degraded performance. If you want us to opt your tenant on your behalf, reply to this thread with the tenant_id and an explicit approval.

Attachments: evacuation-step-by-step.pdf (PDF, 48 KB) — step-by-step enable flow and rollback. temporary-endpoints.csv (CSV) — hostnames and zones to use for manual switch.

We expect to post an initial incident bulletin during the window and a detailed postmortem by 2026-05-21 17:00 UTC. If you have strict compliance requirements (e.g., no cross-region routing), please flag that in your reply and we will coordinate an alternate mitigation path.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Jamie Hayes <platform-ops@bluefin.io>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-19T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Action required: evacuation window for US/EU endpoints — Tenant routing opt-in and reroute steps

Thanks for the heads up, Sofia.

We operate several production tenants across US and EU; tenant IDs: bf-prod-us (us), bf-analytics-eu (eu). We're generally fine allowing emergency reroute, but two asks before we toggle: 1) can you confirm whether any credentials or secrets are passed to the temporary endpoints (we assume no), and 2) can you provide an expected 30-minute maintenance window during which you will validate traffic?

Also, could you opt-in bf-prod-us for us? We can enable bf-analytics-eu via the Console if you confirm the credential question.

Jamie Hayes
Platform Operations — Bluefin Analytics

Subject: Re: Action required: evacuation window for US/EU endpoints — Tenant routing opt-in and reroute steps

Jamie, thanks — answers and next steps below.

1) Credentials/secrets: No secrets or credentials are transmitted to the temporary endpoints. The temporary hostnames act as a routing front that forwards requests to your existing backend without terminating TLS for customer-provided certs. We will not access or log request bodies beyond our normal audit logs. If you have enterprise KMS integration concerns, let us know and we'll validate with Security.

2) Validation window: We will perform the initial canary starting at 2026-05-19 22:15 UTC and expand traffic by stages over a 45-minute window. We will hold at each stage to run health checks and a short latency/5xx check. The full window remains until 02:00 UTC for rollback and cleanup.

3) Opt-in: Per your request we have enabled Emergency Reroute for bf-prod-us (tenant: bf-prod-us). Please verify in Console > Tenant > bf-prod-us > Traffic Routing that the toggle shows "Enabled".

4) Manual fallback: If you prefer manual switching, use the temporary hostnames in temporary-endpoints.csv. We recommend updating DNS TTLs ahead of time to 60 seconds to speed any manual failover.

5) Post-incident and credits: We will publish the preliminary incident note at the end of the window and a full postmortem by 2026-05-21 17:00 UTC. If your availability during the affected window drops below your SLA, we will follow our credit process — contact billing@redwood.com with your tenant_id and affected timestamps.

6) Contacts during the window:
   - Redwood incident lead (on-call): vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
   - Account lead: sofia@redwood.com
   - Escalation / engineering contact: ben_carter@redwood.com

Internal note to team (cc'ed): Vanessa, Ben, Marcus — please monitor bf-prod-us after the canary and escalate to infra if error rates exceed 3% or latency delta > 250ms from baseline. Attachments: evacuation-step-by-step.pdf, temporary-endpoints.csv.

Regards,
Sofia
